ai.description: Rao's Intermediate Golden-backed Frog reaches 35–45 mm. It features a brown dorsum with a distinct golden-yellow mid-dorsal stripe and prominent dorsolateral folds. It lacks a dark temporal mask.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana intermedia* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored dorsolateral fold that contrasts sharply against its dark flanks.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana intermedia* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-altitudes between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Rao's Intermediate Golden-backed Frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours foraging for small invertebrates along the banks of forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana intermedia* breeds during the monsoon, depositing clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs in small, stagnant forest pools or slow-moving streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana intermedia* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting evergreen forests across Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu at moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: *Hylarana intermedia* produces a series of short, high-pitched "tink" or "click" notes, typically heard emanating from vegetation near slow-moving streams in forest habitats.
